llmlang.parser.parse.disposition: added @entry-point/@entry-point(label) recognition (immediately before a named entry header, rejected anywhere else) and → call X / ← return X as content lines valid anywhere a regular - bullet is valid, including nested under decisions/cases/repeats. This is the redesign of the flow feature: flow content now lives directly in ordinary llmlang bullets instead of a separately hand-authored .llmflow file, so there is exactly one place to describe what an entry calls, and nothing to keep in sync by hand.

llmlang.flow.generate_flow.disposition: new entry, replacing the deleted flow_refs()/FlowRef hash-triple system entirely. Composes a .llmflow view purely by walking @entry-point entries and inlining each → call target's own bullets recursively (expanding a given entry only once per trace, so a frequently-called or cyclic function doesn't blow up the render or need re-authoring at every call site). No hashing happens here at all - a → call bullet is just more of its owning entry's text, already covered by that entry's existing text_hash/code_hash.

llmlang.flow.generate_flow_for_tree.disposition: new entry, the tree-walking adapter around generate_flow - builds the entry-point list and per-entry bullet content from a parsed llmlang tree.

llmlang.lockfile_builder.build.disposition: removed all flow-reference hashing/writing; build() now calls the new flow generator and overwrites the sibling .llmflow file unconditionally (same treatment as the lockfile itself), refusing to write anything if a → call target reachable from an @entry-point doesn't resolve.

llmlang.lockfile_builder.finalize.disposition: same change as build() - generates and overwrites .llmflow directly. No flow-specific disposition branch exists anymore: a → call line only ever exists inside some entry's own bullets, so editing one already flags that entry's ordinary SPEC_DIVERGED and goes through the same disposition gate every other bullet edit does.

llmlang.lockfile_checker.check.disposition: removed the flow_refs hash-triple comparison (FLOW_DIVERGED) entirely. check() now regenerates the flow view fresh from the current tree and compares it byte-for-byte against the checked-in .llmflow, reporting FLOW_FILE_STALE on a mismatch - this also catches someone hand-editing the generated file directly, which the old design never could. FLOW_ERROR is kept, now naming the source entry a bad → call line was found in rather than a flow-file line number, since the call now lives in the .llm file, not a separate file.

llmlang.cli.check_one.disposition: bullets now show its two real calls (lockfile_checker.check, and coverage_checker.check_coverage when coverage is active) as → call lines instead of leaving them undescribed.

llmlang.cli.run_check.disposition: bullets now name its real calls (load_config, resolve_coverage, discover_llm_files, check_one, and the text/json report printers) as → call lines instead of leaving the orchestration implicit.

llmlang.cli.run_build.disposition: adds a → call to lockfile_builder.build, naming the delegation that was already true.

llmlang.cli.run_finalize.disposition: adds a → call to lockfile_builder.finalize, naming the delegation that was already true.

llmlang.cli.main.disposition: marked @entry-point (the CLI's own real entry point) and its command dispatch now uses for X case: with a → call to run_check/run_build/run_finalize per case, instead of prose describing the dispatch generically. This entry point is what compiler.llmflow is generated from.
